_meta.indication: VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK is a co-packaged product containing vonoprazan, amoxicillin, and clarithromycin, indicated for the treatment of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1:1), open-label dual therapy, double-blind active-control triple therapy, parallel-group trial comparing vonoprazan triple therapy and vonoprazan dual therapy with lansoprazole triple therapy, 14 days duration
pivotal_trials.population: Male and female adult patients with H. pylori infection, positive with at least 1 of: dyspepsia lasting at least 2 weeks, functional dyspepsia, recent/new non-bleeding peptic ulcer, history of peptic ulcer not treated for H. pylori, or need for long-term NSAID
pivotal_trials.endpoint: H. pylori eradication rate in subjects who did not have a clarithromycin- or amoxicillin-resistant strain at baseline, 4 weeks after end of treatment (mITTp population), confirmed by 13C-urea breath test
pivotal_trials.result: In the mITTp population, eradication rate 84.7% for vonoprazan triple therapy vs 78.8% for lansoprazole triple therapy (difference 5.9%, non-inferior, p<0.0001); vonoprazan dual therapy 78.5% (difference -0.3%, non-inferior, p=0.007). In clarithromycin-resistant (mITTc) subjects, vonoprazan triple therapy 65.8% vs lansoprazole 31.9% (difference 33.8%, 95% CI 17.7% to 48.1%, superior, p<0.0001).

key_safety: For VOQUEZNA TRIPLE PAK the most common adverse reactions (>=2%) were dysgeusia, diarrhea, vulvovaginal candidiasis, headache, abdominal pain, and hypertension. In HP-301, in the triple therapy arm rates were diarrhea 4.0%, dysgeusia 4.6%, vulvovaginal candidiasis 3.2%, headache 2.6%, abdominal pain 2.3%, and hypertension 2.3%. Overall TEAE incidence was 34.1% (triple), 29.9% (dual), and 34.5% (lansoprazole triple).
target_moa: Vonoprazan is a potassium-competitive acid blocker (PCAB) that competitively inhibits the binding of potassium ions to the H+, K+-ATPase (proton pump), suppressing gastric acid secretion; it is co-packaged with the antibacterials amoxicillin (penicillin class) and clarithromycin (macrolide).
modality: small molecule (potassium-competitive acid blocker co-packaged with two small-molecule antibacterials)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the applications did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues unexpected for a drug of this class.

basis.text: Fast track designation was granted on October 21, 2019 (and again January 22, 2021) under IND 143190 for the development of vonoprazan, amoxicillin and clarithromycin for the treatment of H. pylori infection.

On January 22, 2021, the Applicant was granted fast track designation under IND 143190 for the development of vonoprazan tablets, amoxicillin capsules and clarithromycin tablets (copackaged) to be used in combination for the treatment of *H. pylori* infection. Additionally, on January 22, 2021, the Applicant was granted fast track designation under IND 144399 for vonoprazan tablets and amoxicillin

summary.text: These 505(b)(2) NDAs were received September 3, 2021 and reviewed under Priority review, supported by QIDP and fast track designations for the treatment of H. pylori infection. Approval (not accelerated) was based on the pivotal Phase 3 trial HP-301; no advisory committee was convened and no boxed warning or REMS was required.
